newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNAIR TO GAIN OVER FIM 100 MLN ON HOTEL.
newsitem.headline: FINNAIR TO GAIN OVER FIM 100 MLN ON HOTEL.

text.p: Finnish national carrier Finnair Oy CEO Antti Potila said on Monday the airline would gain well over one hundred million markka on the sale of its hotel and restaurant operations.
"For Finnair, this whole deal will mean a result impact of well over one hundred million markka ... this year. It is a non-recurring item," Potila told a news conference.
Finnair said in a statement it was selling a majority of its hotel and restaurant subsidiary, Nordic-Hotel Oy, to Arctia Ltd, a subsidiary of state-owned Alko-Yhtiot Oy.

It said it was also selling the real estate of its Hotel Inter-Continental in Helsinki, valued at 333 million markka, to a new real estate company, in which Finnair will retain a 40 percent stake alongside Alko (41 percent) and engineering group Metra (19 percent).
Finnair said the new real estate company would have a share capital of 400 million markka and that Metra's Hotel Strand Inter-Continental was also being transferred to the new company.
In addition, the airline said it had decided to sell its 49 percent stake in Infa-Hotel Oy, a company which runs the Savoy Hotel in Moscow.
Asked whether Finnair had a buyer for that hotel, Potila said Finnair had only now decided to begin selling the Moscow hotel operations, but that there had been buying interest.
"The company will no lnger have any hotel operations after this measure has been taken," Potila said in a statement.
